title: Electronic Evidence — BSA 2023 and IT Act Interface

content.overview: Electronic records are admissible and proved under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. Section 63 BSA (corresponding to the former Evidence Act s. 65B framework) governs admissibility of electronic records, typically requiring a certificate as to the manner of production and device particulars where the statute so provides. The IT Act gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures; proof of those records in court follows the BSA path. Admissibility is distinct from weight and from substantive liability under the IT Act.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is the item an electronic record? (2) BSA s. 63 certificate/conditions met? (3) Relevance and authenticity separate from admissibility? (4) IT Act recognition vs BSA proof?
content.study:
Never treat a printout or log as automatically proved. Separate relevance, admissibility (BSA), authenticity and weight. IT Act recognition does not bypass BSA proof rules.

No new case invented. Anvar/Arjun Panditrao line is a verification item for the certificate requirement — not expanded as invented holdings here.

sections.heading: Electronic record recognition
sections.body: IT Act confers legal recognition on electronic records and digital signatures for functional equivalence with paper, subject to the Act.

sections.heading: BSA proof path
sections.body: BSA 2023 governs how electronic records are admitted and proved in evidence; s. 63 is the primary electronic-record provision — verify current certificate requirements from the official text.

sections.heading: Certificate
sections.body: Where the statute requires a certificate identifying the electronic record and the manner of production, non-compliance may bar admissibility as secondary electronic evidence.

sections.heading: Admissibility vs weight
sections.body: A record may be admissible yet carry little weight if integrity, chain or authorship is weak.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the record; check BSA conditions; tender certificate if required; argue relevance and weight separately.

provisions.title: Legal recognition of electronic records and signatures

examples.title: Server log
examples.body: Prosecution tenders a server log of unauthorised access — BSA s. 63 conditions and any required certificate must be addressed before the log is treated as proved electronic evidence.

hypotheticals.question: Does IT Act recognition make a WhatsApp chat automatically proved?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Recognition under the IT Act is not a substitute for BSA admissibility and proof requirements.

distinctions.title: IT Act recognition vs BSA proof
distinctions.left: Legal recognition of electronic records/signatures for functional purposes.
distinctions.right: Admissibility and mode of proof in judicial proceedings under BSA.

misconceptions.trap: Any electronic printout is automatically admissible.
misconceptions.correction: BSA conditions, including certificate requirements where applicable, control admissibility.
